title: In a Minnesota tree experiment, mass compensation did not imply survival compensation in fixed species mixtures
abstract: We tested replacement after species arrival with nine tree species in the B4WarmED experiment. We used the balanced 2012 cohort: 3,163 juveniles in 36 plots, six blocks and two Minnesota sites, followed to 2016. For each rain level, we compared warmed and ambient plots. A fixed-performance model gave species equal weights within boreal and temperate groups. The point temperate planting fraction needed to offset boreal living stem mass losses was 23% at +1.6 C and 69% at +3.1 C under ambient rain. Reduced rain gave no mass compensation point. These limits were uncertain and changed with site, cohort and species choice. At +3.1 C under ambient rain, the equal-species reference mixture had 12% less mass but 36% lower survival and a 26-point rise in temperate biomass share. Boreal and temperate survival changes were both negative, so no group fraction maintained survival under their observed mean performance. An exploratory bound allowed any species mixture. Its best point mass-preserving mixture still lost 2.0 survival points under ambient rain and 7.1 under reduced rain, but bootstrap limits crossed zero. Thus the data do not establish that all mixtures fail. The source study already showed boreal decline and temperate growth gains. We add joint mass-survival compensation tests and their uncertainty. Growth can mask a post-arrival survival filter. This does not measure the share of the field climate-tracking gap due to mortality. Only six blocks, nursery juveniles, estimated stem mass, cohort differences and fixed interaction assumptions limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, block draws, figures, source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Warming effects on living stem mass across reference planting fractions. Species weights are equal within boreal and temperate groups, and per-species performance is held fixed. Shading gives pointwise block t intervals with four residual degrees of freedom. The dotted line is the equal-species fraction 5/9. Data: 2012 cohort in B4WarmED, 2016 endpoint.

Total mass and temperate mass share need not give the same result. The reference mixture gives equal initial weight to each species. Bars are site-stratified block bootstrap limits from six blocks. These limits can be narrower than the block t intervals reported in the text.

At +3.1 C, all nine observed species means have lower survival. The hull shows outcomes of any nonnegative mixture under fixed species performance. It shows point estimates, not a confidence region. Crosses mark the best survival changes among mass-preserving mixtures. Bootstrap limits for those bounds cross zero, so universal mixture failure is not established.

citations.reason: Weak community climate tracking motivates an independent experimental test after species arrival. No summaries or estimates from that study enter the analysis.
Species presence dominates spatial thermal gradients. We separate surviving juvenile numbers from living stem mass in an independent experiment.
Bird colonist supply motivates testing what happens after candidate species have been supplied. No bird records are reused.
CC0 source workbook and README from DRUM. Exact files, versions and hashes are in sources.json. Raw data remain external.
Source experiment and original mortality, growth and replacement findings. Our addition is a conditional joint mass-survival mixture test, not the original observation of boreal decline.
Design and performance of the B4WarmED warming system.
